newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WORLDWIDE COMMON LISTINGS RULES NEAR COMPLETION.
newsitem.headline: WORLDWIDE COMMON LISTINGS RULES NEAR COMPLETION.

text.p: An agreement between the world's major stock exchanges on common requirements for companies seeking bourse listings is nearing completion, bringing issuers the hope of cheaper procedures, a senior London Stock Exchange executive said on Wednesday.

Patrick Morton, head of listings at the London Stock Exchange and the British member of an IOSCO working group looking at the issue, told a conference on global accounting in Brussels that core listings standards had already been agreed although barriers stood in the way of their implementation.
"Some existing national requirements will have to be deleted or modified," Morton said.
"In Europe, the European Commission will have to be consulted in order to change the listings directives," he added.

Eventually the listings standards should result in share offering documents that resembled a hybrid of current U.S. and European practices, making it easier and cheaper for companies to organise global issues, or seek secondary quotations in other markets.
For European companies, once separate standards on company accounts were agreed, this would offer them the chance of easier access to the U.S. capital markets.

IOSCO is the international body representing securities markets regulators. The IOSCO working group looking at listings standards was set up in 1987 and comprises representatives of 15 of the worlds largest markets, including New York, London, Frankfurt and Tokyo, Morton said.
Morton said that in the future work could also start on producing common standards for prospectuses covering debt issues.
